messages:
Ivy Chen: Heads up — hit a nasty onboarding edgecase with credential rotation this morning. CLI kept falling back to an org-scoped key after we rotated a project key and the sample app started getting 401s.
Samir Patel: ugh. can you paste the repro? which env vars were set?
Ivy Chen: repro steps: 1) set REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY=proj-old 2) set REDWOOD_ORG_KEY=org-long-lived 3) run sample todo-demo -> works 4) rotate project key (proj-new), export REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY=proj-new 5) immediately run CLI deploy -> CLI used org key instead of new project key, deployed but later requests from app got 401s (project-only tokens).
Ravi Nair: that sounds like credential sourcing order is not stable in the code path that reads env vs config file. CLI should prefer explicit project key over org-wide key. we probably introduced a fallback in an earlier PR to help legacy setups but it's causing surprising behavior during rotation.
Zoe Morales: also seeing SDK parity issues — our JS SDK silently retries on 401 with the same token (which is still org-scoped) and that hides the problem until the app hits rate limits. Should surface a clear error if token scope mismatch is detected.
Samir Patel: can you share the exact commands / logs? a snippet would help.
Ivy Chen: logs: ```bash
$ rw deploy
Using credentials from REDWOOD_ORG_KEY
Deploy successful (but tenant requests later failed)
ERROR: 401 Unauthorized from /v1/models/generate
```
Samir Patel: OK. two separate but related bugs: 1) credential resolution precedence (env/project/config/org) and 2) retry behavior on 401.
Ravi Nair: proposal: canonical precedence = (1) explicit CLI flag (--key) (2) project-scoped env var REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY (3) project in config file (~/.redwood/config -> project.key) (4) REDWOOD_API_KEY / REDWOOD_ORG_KEY as fallback. Document it and enforce in both CLI and SDKs.
Zoe Morales: plus: when token used is org-scoped but the request endpoint requires project scope, we should return a deterministic, early error that includes hint: "token lacks project scope — try REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY or create a project token". Don't swallow it under a retry.
Samir Patel: agreed. Add a short TTL/backoff: if a rotation is detected (env changes between invocations) CLI should prefer the most-recent env var and emit a one-line warning: "Detected changed project key; using REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY (proj-new) — ensure services have rotated."
Ivy Chen: note for sample-apps: they often cache keys in docker images / env files. we should add a devx doc section "rotating keys during onboarding" + a small script that performs zero-downtime swap: create new project token, stage it in app config, flush caches, then switch.
Ravi Nair: action items: Samir -> PR to normalize precedence in CLI; Zoe -> update JS & Python SDKs to stop retrying on 401 and return scope-aware error; Ivy -> draft sample-app doc & rotation script; I'll add unit tests for env-change detection to prevent regressions.
Samir Patel: I'll start the CLI PR today. cc @devex-bot can we add an integration test that simulates env var rotation across process restarts?
devex-bot: Created issue #1423: "Credential precedence + rotation test" and linked to devex board.
Zoe Morales: also recommend we add a small telemetry flag during onboarding (opt-in) that records when a token scope mismatch occurs so we can prioritize UX fixes. nothing PII, just event counts.
Ivy Chen: thanks all — this explains why customer onboarding hit the same problem earlier. once PRs land can someone please ping the #support runbook so CS has an explanation to share?
Samir Patel: will do. I'll post a short changelog blurb and link to the new doc in the PR description.
Ravi Nair: cool — let's aim to have CLI fix + SDK patch in the next patch release.
Zoe Morales: leaving a small note: we should avoid adding yet another env var name. prefer normalizing to REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY and REDWOOD_API_KEY as legacy alias.
Ivy Chen: agreed. thanks team :raised_hands:
